title.narrative: Support for the Ministry of Education Science and Technology School Sector Development Plan (Education SWAp) - Phase 2

description.narrative: (Nepal): The Ministry of Education, Science and Technology (MOEST) has demonstrated its commitment to ensuring equitable access to quality education for all students by meeting targets set under the 2016-2021 School Sector Development Program (SSDP). The MOEST and development partners are developing a new five-year sector plan. In USAID's Education Sector Wide Approach (SWAp) Phase 1, the activity supported one disbursement linked indicator (DLI) that targeted improving primary grade learning outcomes through scale-up of the National Early Grade Reading Program (NEGRP). In SWAp Phase 2, under the new SSDP, USAID will use FY 2020 resources to expand its support to at least two DLI result areas, continuing to incentivize the GON's implementation of targeted interventions to improve primary grade learning outcomes and to ensure that the most marginalized groups have access to education - even in the face of crisis. Potential Phase 2 DLIs include financing targets to expand the NEGRP to the remaining 38 districts, implementing "pro-poor" school interventions that advance Nepal's Equity Strategy, and supporting the continued development of digital distance learning..SWAp Phase 2 advances the USAID key Basic Education Policy priorities: "Children and youth gain literacy, numeracy and social-emotional skills that are foundational to future learning success" and "the most marginalized and vulnerable, have increased access to quality education that is safe and relevant." This assistance will allow the USG to better harmonize foreign development efforts with other donor partners, demonstrate commitment to the principles of aid effectiveness, and achieve financing and Journey to Self-Reliance metrics. This activity supports the Embassy Kathmandu's ICS Goal Two: Increase America's prosperity by developing Nepal as a reliable economic partner and Mission Objective 2.2: Nepal improves health and education outcomes to increase economic productivity..

title.narrative: Strengthening Systems for Better Health (Swasthya ko lagi skakchyam Pranali)

description.narrative: (Nepal): The Strengthening Systems for Better Health (SSBH) activity improves access to sustainable, quality, equitable health services. SSBH supports the GON's new federal structures to promote uninterrupted health service delivery and continuously leverages global experience in health systems strengthening to accelerate improvements in health outcomes. USAID provides technical assistance to the Ministry of Health and Population (MOHP) and provincial and municipal governments to improve access to and use of quality maternal, newborn, and child health; nutrition; water, sanitation, and hygiene; and family planning services in 16 districts. SSBH supports provincial and local governments, and health workers (HWs) to plan, execute, and monitor the health emergency response, including for COVID-19 pandemic and natural disasters. Funding will expand the basic health service package, including nutrition services, to marginalized groups by increasing service delivery points, improving referral mechanisms, and supporting municipalities to improve public and private health services. USAID will train HWs and managers to strengthen the health sector's capacity to generate, analyze, and use real-time data for improved planning and management. Funds will focus on increasing the accountability of local health managers and HWs for quality service delivery by improving linkages among municipal governments, facilities, and patient populations; and leveraging the capacity of Health Facility Operation and Management Committees to make health services more responsive to local needs. .Abt Associates has extensive experience in Nepal and globally in expanding quality health services to vulnerable populations. The activity contributes to USAID/Nepal's CDCS DO3: Inclusive Health and Education Systems Strengthened and Embassy Kathmandu's ICS Goal Two: Increase America's prosperity by developing Nepal as a reliable economic partner..

title.narrative: Reading for All: Disability Inclusion Education for Nepali Children

description.narrative: (Nepal): .While Nepal has achieved universal access to primary education, there remain pockets of marginalized groups - including children with disabilities (CwD) - that do not have access to education. The Reading for All (R4A) activity's objective is to improve reading outcomes for CwD and functional limitations in grades 1-3 in the 16 districts of USAID's Early Grade Reading Program (EGRP). FY 2020 funds will be used to implement an early disability and functional limitation screening tool for students; support the GON to develop a more detailed disability Education Management Information System (EMIS) to improve the quality of data on CwD; implement an education response system and provide necessary referrals; revise national teacher training modules to include support for CwD in early grade reading; and continue supporting teachers on instructional methods for teaching CwD to read. ..Humanity & Inclusion, as a leading implementer on disability programming, is uniquely positioned to apply international learning to the Nepal context in this nascent sub-sector of disability-inclusive education. R4A's emphasis on supporting GON systems to provide equitable access to quality education ultimately contributes to improving key metrics of self-reliance, inclusive development, and government capacity. This activity contributes to Embassy Kathmandu's Integrated Country Strategy Mission Goal Two: Increase America's prosperity by developing Nepal as a reliable economic partner and Mission Objective 2.2, Nepal improves health and education outcomes to increase economic productivity... .

It will closely collaborate with other Feed the Future activities to share methods and practices that have proven successful in managing pests using integrated methods. The activity will expand the scale of its interventions to improve technologies and practices with women and marginalized groups, and train and empower women scientists and plant health professionals. .Virginia Tech University was selected due its technical capacity to implement this intervention in partnership with its Nepal-based sub-awardees and with public and private sector stakeholders. This activity, known as the Suaahara Integrated Nutrition Program, will work in 25 districts using multi-sectorial and community-based nutrition interventions. Likely to expand to an additional 16 districts in 2014, this activity will concentrate on evidence-based, age-appropriate feeding practices such as exclusive breastfeeding, infant and young child feeding, maternal nutrition, essential hygiene actions including safe drinking water and safe disposal of feces, healthy timing and spacing for pregnancy and the dangers of smoking for mothers and their babies. Suaahara also includes a cross-cutting component that aims to increase access to diversified, nutrient-dense food through home-based gardening and poultry farming.

description.narrative: (Nepal): ingha Durbar seeks to mitigate public disillusionment and dissatisfaction towards the Government and political process using multi-media communications and story-telling approaches. Specific project goals include:-- To increase public knowledge of government functions at the local and national levels and foster constructive citizen-government engagement;-- To foster dialogues at multiple levels to create a shared national vision for leadership and governance; and-- To promote positive role models for leadership and governance through popular culture.The initiative centers on the production and broadcast of 13-episodes of a political TV drama series, Singha Durbar, and a 52-episode radio drama series, Gaun Gaunma Singha Durbar. It uses these two media products in addition to think tank events and policy papers to catalyze dialogue among key stakeholders on governance, collaborative leadership, and policy issues in Nepal. This is expected to increase public understanding of how government works at local and national levels, increase interest in constructive civic engagement, and help identify possibilities for collaborative political culture in Nepal. By neutralizing partisanship and conflicting points of view by portraying issues in the form of a story with the public as observers, the project aims to build trust and promote values of inclusion, transparency, honesty and collaborative government through good leadership by creating role models. The media products developed will reach citizens in in all 75 districts through local FM stations.The project is implemented by Search For Common Ground (SFCG) in partnership with the Antenna Foundation, Common Ground Productions and local contractors for the production of radio and television dramas.

description.narrative: (Nepal): The Swachchhata activity improves hygiene conditions and practices in healthcare facilities (HCF) across four districts of Nepal's Province 6; strengthens the Ministry of Health and Population's (MOHP).capacity to maintain infection prevention (IP) and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) standards in HCFs; and improves community hygiene behaviors. Using FY 2019 funds, USAID will complete construction of water supply, toilet facilities, waste management, and electrical installation for selected facilities. To ensure sustainability of these structures, USAID will train Health Facility Operations and Management Committees (HFOMCs) on governance and maintenance procedures. USAID will also train healthcare providers and community health volunteers to incorporate hygiene messages during health counseling sessions. This training will also include an advocacy module to help health staff secure funds from HFOMCs to procure supplies and equipment. Funds will also be used to train HFOMCs on monitoring the effectiveness of hygiene communication by health workers, including how to conduct client satisfaction exit surveys. Overall, the activity will contribute to the Government of Nepal's journey to self-reliance by strengthening commitment and capacity to improve health outcomes and ensuring a healthy and productive workforce. USAID will leverage SNV's global WASH expertise to improve Nepal's national WASH standards in HCFs in support of Embassy Kathmandu's Integrated Country Strategy Mission Goal Two: Increase America's prosperity by developing Nepal as a reliable economic partner and Mission Objective 2.2, Nepal improves health and education outcomes to increase economic productivity..

(Nepal): Suahaara II focuses on the 1,000-day period between conception and a child's second birthday as a critical window to shaping a child's cognitive and physical development through improved nutrition. With FY 2021 funds, the activity will continue to reduce the prevalence of stunting, underweight, and wasting among children; improve household health, nutrition and water, sanitation and hygiene behaviors and practices; increase the use of quality health services; increase the consumption of diverse and nutritious foods by women and their families; and support counseling and behavior change communication on family planning in mothers' groups. Suaahara II will work with the GON in 389 of the 753 municipalities in Nepal using evidence-based, multi-sectoral nutrition interventions at the policy, community, and household levels. Suaahara II will improve health and nutrition behaviors and reduce the impact of health emergencies such as COVID-19 on health and nutrition by strengthening community health systems. This will include training health facility staff on the promotion of exclusive breastfeeding, infant and young child feeding, maternal and newborn care, integrated management of acute malnutrition and childhood illness, and maternal and adolescent nutrition. In addition, it will promote essential hygiene actions (e.g., safe drinking water, disposal of feces), healthy timing and spacing of pregnancy, and provide information on family planning methods and service availability..This activity will utilize $50,000 of the $5 million Water earmark..Helen Keller International has vast experience implementing integrated nutrition interventions essential to achieve the goals of the activity. Improving nutritional health ensures a healthy and productive workforce in support of Embassy Kathmandu's ICS Goal Two: Increase America's prosperity by developing Nepal as a reliable economic partner..

Objectives for Nepal: Promote key Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) practices through an intensivebehavior change strategy, including interpersonal communication activities, radio programs, and theuse of mobile technology at the community level. Expand coverage of the community-based integrated management of newborn and childhood illnessprogram and strengthen growth monitoring and promotion at outreach clinics and health facilities. Enhance clean water, sanitation, and hygiene conditions of household facilities and establish privatesector linkages to promote WASH technologies. Improve consumption of nutritious food through increased production, improved post-harveststorage, and processing diverse nutritious food, especially for women farmers from disadvantagedgroups. Strengthen coordination on health and nutrition between government and other stakeholdersthrough the Food Security and Nutrition Coordination Committee, Nepal Nutrition Group,Nutrition Technical Committee, Safe Motherhood sub- committee, Family Planning Sub -committee,and Reproductive Health Coordination Committee. Strengthen the technical, managerial, operational capacity of health and non-health sectorstakeholders at the district and Village Development Committee (VDC) levels to enhance MSNPimplementation.

COVID-19 interventions will focus on citizen advocacy, countering disinformation, and engagement with the government to improve service delivery..FHI 360 has worked for over two decades in Nepal to improve public awareness, promote the use of social accountability, and advance the institutional sustainability of CSOs and the media. Strengthen organizational capacity and sustainability of CSO and media working in USAID priority sectors.

title.narrative: Hariyo Ban II (Green Forests II) Program

description.narrative: (Nepal): USAID's Hariyo Ban II activity reduces threats to biological diversity and the impacts of climate change within two conservation landscapes: Terai Arc Landscape (TAL) and Chitwan Annapurna Landscape (CHAL) covering 40 percent of Nepal. It applies an integrated landscape perspective to biodiversity conservation and sustainable forests and watersheds management in partnership with community groups in four biodiversity corridors in TAL and three sub-river basins in CHAL that complement policy support at federal, provincial, and local levels. .With FY 2019 funds, Hariyo Ban II will provide technical assistance to improve the management of 200,000 hectares of biodiverse forests and buffer zones surrounding national parks. It will support conservation and enterprise activities benefiting over 10,000 people. USAID will invest in risk reduction activities that build resilience, benefiting about 30,000 people, and will integrate gender equity and social inclusion considerations into the policies of 100 forest user groups. The activity will safeguard biological diversity, combat wildlife crime, and promote judicious use of natural resources, thereby preserving Nepal's long-term economic prospects. .USAID/Nepal awarded the activity to World Wide Fund for Nature because of its technical expertise in managing natural resources development activities and its long established working relationships with host-country government and non-government stakeholders. The activity builds self-reliance and advances key objectives of the U.S. Government's Indo-Pacific Strategy by addressing threats to biodiversity and supporting resilience-building measures. Hariyo Ban II contributes to Embassy Kathmandu's ICS Goal Two: Increase America's prosperity by developing Nepal as a reliable economic partner, and Mission Objective 2.3, Nepal establishes environmentally sustainable practices and demonstrates increased capacity to safeguard natural resources..

Objectives for Nepal: EXPECTED BIODIVERSITY RESULTS: Increase in Tiger 198 > 52; Rhino 645 > 55; Snow Leopard 51 > 20; ‘O’ tiger poaching >2; Over 500,000 (50,000 in hba) ha forest area will be under improved management. Over 20,000 people will be trained on conservation and.forest management. Over 30,000 people will get increased economic benefits from NRM.

(Nepal): USAID's works to Combat Trafficking in Persons (CTIP) through the Hamro Samman (HS) activity that partners with the GON, civil society, and private sector partners to strengthen key relationships among stakeholders. The lack of coordination among the GON, civil society, and private sector, combined with the dearth of effective data collection and sharing among stakeholders continues to make Nepal an attractive environment for traffickers, exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. HS will use $1,500,000 of FY 2021 CTIP-earmarked funds and $100,000 of the Women, Peace and Security directive to: strengthen an integrated data collection system at the national and sub-national levels; provide technical assistance to national and local CTIP committees and help CSOs with data collection, analysis, and communication; facilitate information sharing among CSOs, government, and law enforcement; form private sector partnerships to expand access to quality services for trafficking survivors and at-risk groups; strengthen CTIP advocacy plans; provide shelter and counselling services for the reintegration of trafficking victims; and expand access to legal resources for survivors. In response to COVID-19, HS will equip shelters with materials needed for infection prevention and control to protect the resident survivors and other shelter staff from infection. .Winrock International is best placed to meet USAID's goals in CTIP as it has 30 years of experience working with governments to leverage CTIP data through evidence-based policy and survivor services. By strengthening national and local level CTIP capacity, Nepal will be better able to disrupt criminal networks, reduce rights violations, and decrease regional and U.S. bound trafficking and human smuggling. HS supports Embassy Kathmandu's ICS Goal One: Promote American Security by supporting a stable, secure, democratic and sovereign Nepal..

Objectives for Nepal: The project aims to strengthen Committees to Control Human Traffic at district and national level to collect and use trafficking data for better policy, enforcement and services; reach at-risk individuals through media campaigns; Government and CSO partners with improved capacity to deliver TIP services; Private sector partnerships actively providing services and referrals through TIP networks; at-risk individuals will have increased entrepreneurial skills and employment opportunities

title.narrative: Knowledge-based Integrated Sustainable Agriculture and Nutrition Project-II (KISAN II)

description.narrative: (Nepal): KISAN IIis a flagship activity under the Global Food Security Strategy (GFSS) that provides technical assistance to increases resilience, inclusiveness, and sustainable income growth of small-holder farmers in 21 hill and Terai districts of Nepal's Western, Midwestern, and Far-Western regions; and four earthquake affected districts. The implementing partner, Winrock International, is well positioned to achieve GFSS goals given its extensive experience implementing GFSS activities in Asia using a market systems approach to increase the ability of vulnerable farm households to respond to market opportunities, a core strategy adopted under KISAN II. KISAN II develop local market systems for rice, maize, lentils, high-value vegetables, and goats through technical assistance to farmers to access productivity-enhancing and improved post-harvest practices and technologies; and by strengthening extension services through introduction of new technologies and business models to improve storage, mechanization, input supply, and finance. KISAN II will administer a $1.5 million grants program to foster partnerships with 125 private firms and cooperatives in order to provide market-based solutions to improve agricultural productivity and market access for 130,000 farming households. KISAN II will work with the Ministry of Agriculture and relevant departments to provide an evidence base that will inform policy formulation to create a favorable business enabling environment. These interventions will contribute to the GFSS overall goal of sustainably reducing hunger, malnutrition and poverty through nutrition-sensitive approaches, which directly contributes to Embassy Kathmandu's Integrated Country Strategy (ICS) Objective 2.1: Nepal advances inclusive and sustainable economic growth to reduce extreme poverty and increase rules-based trade, competitiveness, and cross-border cooperation, and becomes a reliable economic partner for increased American prosperity.

(Nepal): USAID's Health for Life (H4L) Logistics project aims to strengthen the Ministry of Health and Population (MOHP) Logistics Management Division's (LMD) existing systems to ensure the sustained availability of essential health commodities in facilities throughout Nepal. In FY 2015, USAID will work to decentralize logistics management. This includes the expansion of the pull system for commodity distribution and the web-based logistics management information system for commodity inventory, especially in the area of family planning and HIV products as well as essential maternal and child health commodities. USAID will also help facilitate the integration of the logistics system between disparate divisions of the Ministry of Health, including the HIV/AIDS center. USAID funds will also be used to enhance the capacity of the MOHP's Logistic Management Division and improve human and institutional capacities to perform core logistics functions.

Objectives for Nepal: Expand Web-based LMIS down to health facilities in selected districts. Strengthen the distribution system in health centers across the supply chain, so that each level of the supply chain works in concert with the other levels. Support collaboration between the HIV/AIDS logistics system and national health logistics system to identify challenges and opportunities for systems integration. Work with districts to facilitate contracting out for the transportation of health commodities to health facilities using private transporters for efficiency and effectiveness. Enhance the LMD’s capacity for human resource management, monitoring and evaluation, planning, budgeting, and supply chain management activities including forecasting, logistics management information system, procurement planning, quality assurance, storage, and distribution. H4L Logistics will support the Government of Nepal to achieve the following results: Health facilities at the district level and below empowered to make informed decisions about the commodities supply based on local needs Vulnerable groups, women, girls, and newborns receive improved HIV services through greater efficiency in HIV/AIDS logistics management. The national supply chain system continues to reduce stock-outs and wastage.

description.narrative: (Nepal): USAID/Nepal's Business Literacy Program is a major component of the Feed the Future Strategy in Nepal. The primary objective of the Business Literacy Program is to increase the resilience of vulnerable households and communities through enhanced literacy, numeracy and business/entrepreneurial skills. The program provides entrepreneurial literacy training to 48,000 beneficiaries from vulnerable groups, defined as women, ethnic minorities, disadvantaged castes and youth. These beneficiaries are a subset of beneficiaries from the primary Feed the Future project, the Knowledge-based Integrated Sustainable Agriculture and Nutrition (KISAN) project. The Business Literacy Program is geographically targeted in 20 Terai and lower hill districts in the Far-Western, Mid-Western, and Western Regions of Nepal.The three key program elements are: 1) developing business literacy training materials; 2) conducting a training of trainers program; and 3) delivering business literacy training to beneficiaries. Project beneficiaries attend a year-long training program two hours per day, six days per week.USAID's Business Literacy Program in Nepal will use $400,000 from FY 2015 funds to provide enhance entrepreneurial literacy training to beneficiaries.

description.narrative: Through the Sabal project, USAID will help vulnerable individuals, households (HHs), and communities in six districts in the Central Hills and the Eastern Hills of Nepal by:(1) reducing the exposure of HHs and communities to agricultural, public health, or climate-related hazards, and enhancing the ability to cope with shocks, (2) identifying adaptive innovations to help HHs and communities adjust to major trends, such as climate change or the expansion of markets into rural areas, and (3) developing a discrete number of promising innovations that will drive scalable improvement in people's lives.
